ai.title: Remove bunx --bun flag from internal drizzle-kit scripts
ai.summary: Reverts `bunx --bun` wrapper in `packages/internal/package.json` for `db:generate`, `db:migrate`, and `db:studio`. Scripts now call `drizzle-kit` directly. Corresponding documentation explaining `.env.local` loading behavior in `packages/internal/knowledge.md` is deleted. Affects internal database tooling only.

eli5.text: When you run certain helper commands that work with your internal database (like setting up the database tables or opening the database browser), they now run a little bit differently under the hood. Previously, these commands were routed through a compatibility tool that made sure your secret configuration files were loaded correctly. Now, they call the underlying tool more directly. You likely won't notice anything different when running these commands, but if you do, it could mean those commands no longer automatically read your local settings file.

ai.title: fetchUsageData test uses DI instead of process.env
ai.summary: fetchUsageData test passes clientEnv via DI instead of deleting process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL. Refactors test to avoid mutating global env. Updates cli/src/hooks/__tests__/use-usage-query.test.ts.

eli5.text: The automated checks that verify the assistant's usage-reporting feature now pass configuration directly into the test instead of temporarily deleting and restoring a global setting. This matters only to the people who maintain the assistant's source code, it stops the tests from accidentally leaking one experiment's configuration into another. If you glanced at the test file, you'd see the app-url absence is now simulated by handing the test a deliberately incomplete settings object, rather than erasing and later re-adding a shared environment value.

ai.title: Fix env var inheritance for bun script subprocesses
ai.summary: Updated .bin/bun to explicitly pass --env-file flags to subprocesses, ensuring tools like drizzle-kit inherit environment variables. Bun's native .env loading fails to propagate vars to child script processes, causing runtime errors in worktree environments. Scope covers the bun wrapper and scripts/init-worktree.ts, which now merges base branch HEAD to guarantee latest tooling sync. Precedence order remains .env.local then .env.development.local.

eli5.text: When the system runs helper tools (like the database migration tool) behind the scenes, they now correctly receive all the secret settings they need to function, instead of running with missing configuration and failing. Previously, the launch script would set up the environment files correctly, but Bun's automatic loading did not pass those settings down to the smaller tool programs, causing them to error out in worktree environments. Now the launch script explicitly tells each helper tool which configuration files to use, ensuring settings flow from the main project into every tool that needs them. This is live today and affects anyone running these tools in worktree setups.

ai.title: Fix direnv allow prompt in init-worktree script
ai.summary: Scripts/init-worktree.ts now invokes direnv allow via bash -c with explicit cd, replacing the previous runCommand call that failed to pass correct directory context. The change ensures direnv sees the intended worktree path, preventing silent failures or incorrect environment loading. Scope limited to internal tooling scripts. Error handling distinguishes between missing bash and other failures, resolving the promise regardless of outcome.

eli5.text: When you ask the computer to open a new copy of a project and prepare it for you to work on, it now uses a small helper program to set up your environment correctly instead of trying to do it directly. Previously, this helper sometimes ran in the wrong folder, so the setup didn't apply to the new copy you were opening. Now it makes sure to switch to the right folder first before running. This only affects people who start new copies of the project behind the scenes.

ai.title: Fix typecheck in use-usage-query test
ai.summary: Updated `use-usage-query.test.ts` to use `as unknown as ClientEnv` instead of direct casting for `clientEnv` mock. This resolves a typecheck failure caused by strict type incompatibility between the mock object and `ClientEnv` interface. Scope limited to CLI test file.

eli5.text: The assistant's test helper that checks usage reports had a small mismatch in how it passed in environment settings, which caused a type-check failure during automated testing. The tool now uses a standard double-step cast instead of a direct one, so the test suite passes cleanly. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping for the CLI's internal tests, you wouldn't notice anything different in your day-to-day use.

ai.title: ask-user redesigns option focus, keyboard hints, shared constants
ai.summary: The ask-user CLI form overhauls option rendering: focused options now use `theme.primary` background with inverted text and bold attributes, while selection state drives color independently. `getOptionLabel`, `OTHER_OPTION_INDEX`, and a new `KEYBOARD_HINTS` array move to `constants.ts`, de-duplicating helpers from `index.tsx` and `accordion-question.tsx`. Question numbering and option indentation are computed dynamically from `questionPrefix.length` rather than hardcoded. Hover-focus suppression via `suppressNextHoverFocusRef` and terminal-focus gating through `useChatStore` prevent unintended focus changes during mouse interaction.

eli5.text: When you're asked a question in the terminal and you use the arrow keys or hit Enter, the way options look as you move through them just got cleaner. The selected choice now stands out with a highlighted background and bold text, and the keyboard hints at the bottom tell you exactly which keys do what (arrows to move, Enter to pick, Esc to skip). These are visible right now the next time the assistant asks you to select from a list of answers.
